messages:
deploy-bot: Starting rollout wave 2 -> us-west-2 for service: inference-gateway (rev=release-2026-03-17). Canary config: 5% traffic, healthchecks enabled.
incident-bot: Alert: Elevated 5xx rate detected on inference-gateway (us-west-2) — 4.8% 5xx over 2m, latency p95 820ms. Trigger: canary-health-threshold.
sara: paging on-call. seeing 5xx climb on canary, pulling into thread.
mike: I’m on it, joining. looking at logs now. any client reports?
ana: (via cust-monitor) A small subset of customers intermittently seeing failures when streaming large responses.
tara: checking autoscaler + kv cache metrics — kv-cache miss rate spiked around the same time as 5xx bump.
mike: grep from the canary pod logs: ```
ERROR: kv-cache: evict failed, OOMError
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/opt/service/serve.py", line 392, in handle_request
    result = model.generate(...)
OOMError: kernel launch failed
```
incident-bot: Pager: oncall@sre notified (severity=high).
sara: hypothesis: quantized model OOM on certain token lengths causing 502s -> fallback path returns 5xx. recommend kill-switch to cut canary.
brian: we should toggle the rollout flag first (no full rollback yet) — flip canary-traffic to 0% and route to baseline model.
leo: +1, do we have the feature flag command ready?
mike: ready. command: ```/ops flip-flag canary-traffic --env=prod --value=0 --reason="rapid 5xx canary"```
sara: doing it now. /ops flip-flag canary-traffic --env=prod --value=0 --reason="rapid 5xx canary"
deploy-bot: Feature flag canary-traffic set to 0% (user: sara). Applying routing changes — shifting traffic to stable model (rev=release-2026-03-10).
incident-bot: Observability update: 1m after flag flip 5xx dropped to 0.9%, p95 latency back to 220ms.
tara: confirming kv-cache evictions normalized and memory usage on canary hosts trending down. looks like OOM was the trigger.
ana: cust-success: no major customer-impact alerts yet; a few error reports from alpha customers, but auto-retries covered.
sara: good. I'll keep the flag off and roll back the canary release. mike/tara, let's schedule a postmortem and capture the prompt shapes that hit the OOM.
mike: I’ll grab traces + heap dumps from the canary nodes and add to the incident doc.
brian: filing rollback ticket and tagging oncall-sre for follow-up. ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-ROLLBACK-6123
sara: handing off to next oncall for monitoring through the evening: @leo you’re the remote oncall, please watch the dashboards until 23:00 PT.
leo: acknowledged, I’ll watch and ping if anything changes.
incident-bot: Incident closed (auto): mitigation applied -> canary traffic cut, rollback initiated. Severity downgraded to informational.
sara: short postmortem checklist: capture trigger, reproduce with long-token prompt, add kvcache guardrails, add canary memory SLO alarms, and test quantized kernel at scale before next rollout. assigning owners in the doc. :memo: :white_check_mark:
